data.title: Validation
data.tagline: Check that incoming data has the expected shape and allowed values
data.description: A required field can be checked when someone leaves it, while cross-field rules usually need a submit-time check. Frontend feedback helps people correct mistakes, but the backend must validate again and return specific field errors.

use: Validate form submissions on the server
Return field-level errors the interface can explain
avoid: Trust data only because TypeScript compiled
Return one vague error for every field
Use validation as a substitute for authentication or authorization

lessonPractice.title: A signup form accepts the age “twenty”. Which handling is more reliable?

options.label: Give browser feedback and validate the type and range again on the server
options.feedback: Correct. Browser feedback helps people fix input; server validation is the final check that cannot be bypassed.

options.label: Save whenever the browser input restricts the field to numbers
options.feedback: Browser restrictions can be bypassed or skipped by a direct API call.

options.label: Save the original text and have operations clean invalid values later
options.feedback: Invalid data should be rejected or corrected before it enters later workflows.

data.agentPrompt: The signup endpoint accepts invalid ages. Keep the immediate browser feedback and add server-side type and range validation. Submit one valid age and “twenty”: the valid request should create a record, while the invalid one should return a readable error and create none.
